**Linux** — `flatpak install ruze-0.0.31.flatpak`, then `flatpak run com.ruze.chat`.

---

### Added

- **You can call a friend from a conversation.** There is a camera beside
  their name; pressing it rings them, and their window says who is calling
  with Answer and Dismiss. Answering opens the same call a server room opens —
  the same tiles, the same mute, camera, screen share and hang up — so
  everything that works in a room works between two people.

  Ringing is a room appearing rather than a message being sent. If they are in
  one and you are not, they are calling; if it goes, they have hung up, and it
  goes on its own because a room exists only while somebody is in it. There is
  no invite to get lost and no answer to arrive twice, and a call cannot end up
  open on one side and closed on the other.

  It needed no new agreement between the two of you. A conversation is two
  documents — each person writes their own half — and both of you hold both
  ids, so the call happens on the smaller of the two. Each side works that out
  alone, at any time, with nothing exchanged.

  It rings, and the ring is a ring rather than a chime. Everything else Ruze
  plays is a soft two- or three-note bell that acknowledges something; this is
  four clipped electronic pulses on a rising minor third, repeating every
  second and a half until you answer or dismiss it. A minor interval does not
  resolve, so it never sounds finished — which is the point of a sound that is
  going to ask again. It can be turned off with the others in Settings, and
  like every sound here it is synthesised rather than a file, so there is
  nothing to download before the first call.

  Dismiss puts the ring away on your side. It does not tell them anything,
  because nothing here can stop somebody choosing to call — and a button that
  implied otherwise would be lying about what it does.
